criterion_scores.reasoning: All 5 numbered YED-223 decisions verified against actual behavior, not comments: (1) both gemini-judge.sh and openai_judge.py exit 2 with a clear message when --context/--spec-file accompany --bundle, confirmed by test + manual run; (2) judge_lib.py bundle prints an unmissable stderr EVIDENCE-PARITY WARNING when evidence_parity is false, confirmed by a dedicated test asserting it fires at 0 chars and stays quiet at 500; (3) gemini-judge.sh's bundle-mode parity message now explicitly says 'no seat flag can fix it'; (4) test_adapter_contract.py's new block exercises the bundle-refusal path for both CLI-adapter seats (gemini, openai) via the shared `seats` list; (5) verify_quotes correctly restricts tolerant matching to PROSE_TYPES, never alters `_`, and I could not get any fabricated quote to verify in code/hook/unknown modes nor construct a semantically-different fabrication that verifies in prose mode via adversarial probing beyond the shipped tests. The only thing found (defect 1) is a documentation cross-reference to the wrong SKILL.md step number, which doesn't affect behavior.

Every artifact touched by the spec is present: both adapters, judge_lib.py (verify_quotes signature + bundle-time warning), seat-log.py (now passes artifact_type), two test files with new coverage, and the reference doc + SKILL.md updated to describe the new behavior. No TODOs, no stubs. Two minor gaps filed as defects: (a) the SKILL.md guidance for decision 2 sits in Step 1 rather than the Step 2 the decision names; (b) the new doc prose describes quote-tolerance as an 'adapters' (plural) feature without noting Gemini's schema carries no `quote` field and is therefore not covered by verify_quotes at all. Neither is load-bearing and no referenced file/rubric/doc is missing (bundle's own VERIFIED-MISSING REFERENCES = none), so no cap applies.

House conventions followed throughout: files stay in their existing correct locations (.claude/hooks/, .claude/evals/, .claude/references/, .claude/skills/judge-build/) with no naming or prefix violations; the SDK constraint that subagents can't spawn subagents and that MCP writes are parent-thread-only is untouched and not violated (no subagent/MCP code in this diff); source-of-truth discipline is respected — evidence parity is fixed at the bundle-build step and the fix propagates by reference (comments and doc point back to judge_lib.build_bundle) rather than being reimplemented per adapter. No tombstoned decision (Supabase-as-measurement-store, gtm-os, Langfuse) is touched or resurrected.

The fix is narrowly scoped to exactly what round 1 and round 2 got wrong (documented inline with concrete incident references — the false-FLAG-on-a-skill-file case, and the hay_loose/__init__/*args/--bundle fabrications from earlier rounds), with no speculative surface added beyond that. No duplicated state (bundle remains the single evidence artifact; parity is computed once at build time and read, not recomputed per seat). No fabricated numbers or orphan metrics introduced. The residual limitation (prose quotes differing only by the protected punctuation classes still verify) is recorded in the code comment and the reference doc rather than hidden, which is the honest version of 'lean, not gold-plated.'

Comments are unusually concrete and falsifiable: each regex decision cites the specific prior failure it fixes (a Sonnet seat's dropped ** and em-dash-as-colon causing a false FLAG; round 1/2 letting hay_loose/__init__/_private/*args/--bundle verify). Failures are loud (adapters exit non-zero with an explanatory message rather than silently dropping flags), and the 'Recorded residual' language is an honest admission of the tolerant-mode's known limit rather than an overclaim. The one gap (defect 2) is that the new doc text doesn't disclose that the Gemini seat isn't quote-checked at all, which is a minor omission in an otherwise honest set of docs, not a false claim of a property the code doesn't have.

defects.quote: **Evidence parity is fixed HERE, at build time** (YED-223).
defects.issue: Spec decision (2) says 'the judge-build SKILL Step 2 says to rebuild the bundle with --spec-file rather than re-run a seat.' The added guidance actually lands under Step 1 ('Build ONE evidence bundle') at line 265, not Step 2 ('Run the three seats in parallel', unchanged). The substance (rebuild, don't re-run a seat) is fully present and arguably better placed where the bundle is actually built, but it doesn't literally match the decision's own step reference — a documentation-location nit, not a logic gap.
defects.decision: pass-with-minor, not capped (substance present, location mismatch only)

defects.quote: Quote verification is format-tolerant for prose only.
defects.issue: This new reference text (and SKILL.md's Step 3 addition at line 271) describes the tolerant-quote fix as applying to 'seat-log.py and the adapters.' I read gemini-judge.sh's request SCHEMA (its defects object requires only location/criterion/severity/spec_ref/description) and confirmed it has no `quote` field at all and never calls verify_quotes — grep across .claude/ confirms verify_quotes is only invoked by seat-log.py (Claude/Sonnet) and openai_judge.py (OpenAI). The Gemini seat has zero quote verification, tolerant or strict. The new prose doesn't say this, so a reader could believe quote-fabrication defense is uniform across all three seats when it's actually two of three.
defects.decision: pass-with-minor, not capped (pre-existing condition, not introduced by this diff; doesn't affect correctness of what was actually changed)

checks_performed: Read judge-system-v2 rules and build-quality@5 rubric in full before scoring.
Checked the diff's behavior against each of YED-223's 5 numbered decisions individually, reading the actual changed code (not just comments/docstrings).

In the harness worktree (alex/yed-223-judge-harness, HEAD=c655be3), sourced .env and ran python3 .claude/evals/test_judge_lib.py (47/47 pass), test_adapter_contract.py (39/39 pass), test_quorum_scenarios.py (6/6 pass), test_quorum_nseat.py (40/40 pass) — all green, including the new YED-223 cases.
Confirmed openai-judge.sh is a thin `exec python3 openai_judge.py "$@"` shim, so the contract test's --bundle-refusal loop genuinely exercises openai_judge.py's new refusal branch, not a mock.

Read seats.json and test_adapter_contract.py's `seats` filter (`runner` ending in .sh/.py) and confirmed it correctly scopes decision 4's 'every seat' to the two CLI-adapter seats (gemini, openai), excluding the Agent-dispatched Claude/Sonnet seat (runner:'agent'), which has no CLI flags to refuse in the first place.

Called judge_lib.verify_quotes directly with adversarial inputs targeting the dangerous direction (fabricated quote verifying as real): cross-sentence concatenation across two dash-delimited fragments, clause-reordering around dash tokens, colon-list causal-claim fabrication ('revenue: growth' -> 'revenue causes growth'), backtick-identifier substitution, and a prose-mode attempt to turn `--bundle` into `: bundle` via the dash/colon swap (protected — unspaced double-hyphen is never touched) — all correctly rejected (unverified=1) in prose (skill/ref) and code/hook modes.

Confirmed legitimate format variants (dropped **/backticks, em-dash-as-colon, spaced-hyphen-as-em-dash, and a combination of both in one quote) correctly verify in prose mode, and that the exact-match count (unverified_exact) still reflects the underlying literal mismatch.
Confirmed 'ref' and 'dossier' types get prose-tolerant matching and 'code'/'hook'/unknown(None) get strict matching, matching PROSE_TYPES exactly as named in the addendum.

Grepped every call site of verify_quotes() in the repo (seat-log.py, openai_judge.py, test files) to confirm all real callers were updated to pass artifact_type; confirmed the new default (artifact_type=None) fails safe to strict matching for any caller that wasn't updated.

Checked judge_lib.build_bundle()'s evidence_parity threshold (len(ctx) >= 400) matches gemini-judge.sh's own CTX_LEN<400 threshold, and that the new _cli() build-time warning reads the same b['evidence_parity'] field the bundle already carried.

Verified via the bundle's own VERIFIED-MISSING REFERENCES and LIVE REFERENCES TO REMOVED TOOLS/DECISIONS sections that check-refs.sh and check-tombstones.py found nothing against this artifact (both '(none)').
Scanned the diff for hardcoded secrets, stray debug output, or TODO stubs — none found.

Confirmed file placement/executable bits are unchanged and correct (gemini-judge.sh, openai_judge.py, seat-log.py remain in .claude/hooks/; SKILL.md stays under .claude/skills/judge-build/ with no alex: prefix).
